transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I keep getting dizzy when I stand up. It's been happening for a little while now, and it worries me.
Do you have any allergies, or have you ever had a bad reaction to a medicine?
No, I've never had a bad reaction to anything as far as I know. No allergies.
How bad is the dizziness when you stand up?
It's not too bad — uncomfortable, but I can manage. It does make me grab hold of something sometimes.
Could you tell me what medicines you take, including any new or changed ones, and how much you take if you know?

I take a water tablet for my blood pressure, and a small one for my stomach each morning — I can't remember what that one's called. There's paracetamol for my hips. And the nurse started me on a new blood pressure tablet a little while back. I don't really know the amounts, sorry.
Besides your blood pressure and stomach, do you have any other long-term health conditions?
I've got arthritis in both hips, which is why I take the paracetamol. And I've had high blood pressure for years, about fifteen now.
When the dizziness comes on, does anything else happen at the same time?
No, nothing like that — no chest pain or palpitations, and I haven't blacked out. My arms and legs feel fine.
When the dizziness comes on, where in your body do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere else?
It's mostly in my head, a swimmy sort of feeling. No, it doesn't spread anywhere — it's just that about-to-faint feeling.
How often does the dizzy feeling happen when you stand up?
It happens a few times, on and off. I haven't really counted.
When did you first notice this dizzy feeling when you stand up?
It started a little while back, not long after the new tablet. I can't say exactly when.
You've mentioned arthritis and high blood pressure — is there anything else about your past health that you think I should know?
No, I don't think so. That's about it really — the hips and the blood pressure.
Is there anything else about the medicines you take that you think I should know?
The nurse added the new one because my readings were still high. The water tablet I've been on for years, and the little stomach one too. I'm sorry, I don't remember the names of them.
Thinking back to when this first began, did it come on suddenly, or did it build up gradually over time, or are you not sure?
It came on gradually, over a few days. It wasn't all at once, just started happening after I'd been on the new tablet for about a week.
How bad is the dizziness when you stand up — is it mild, moderate, or severe, or are you not sure?
I'd say it's moderate — I'd put it at about a six out of ten. It's bad enough that I nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop.
Besides the tablets you've already told me about, is there anything else you take for your health — like something you buy at the chemist, a cream or patch, or a vitamin?
No, nothing like that. Just what I've told you about.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
